title.en: Atomic spectra and Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom
title.kn: ಪರಮಾಣು ರೋಹಿತಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಹೈಡ್ರೋಜನ್ ಪರಮಾಣುವಿನ ಬೋರ್ ಮಾದರಿ

hook.en: Sprinkle common salt on a gas flame and it flashes yellow; copper gives green. Every element gives its own set of bright lines, like a fingerprint. Bohr used hydrogen’s lines to build his model of the atom.
hook.kn: ಉಪ್ಪನ್ನು ಅನಿಲ ಜ್ವಾಲೆಗೆ ಹಾಕಿದರೆ ಹಳದಿ ಹೊಳಪು ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ; ತಾಮ್ರ ಹಸಿರು ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಧಾತುವೂ ಬೆರಳಚ್ಚಿನಂತೆ ತನ್ನದೇ ರೇಖೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೈಡ್ರೋಜನ್ ರೇಖೆಗಳಿಂದ ಬೋರ್ ತಮ್ಮ ಮಾದರಿಯನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸಿದರು.

objectives.en: Name the series of the hydrogen spectrum
Calculate energies, radii and wavelengths for hydrogen-like species

narration.en: Sprinkle common salt on a gas flame and it flashes yellow; copper gives green. Every element gives its own set of bright lines, like a fingerprint. Bohr used hydrogen’s lines to build his model of the atom.
narration.kn: ಉಪ್ಪನ್ನು ಅನಿಲ ಜ್ವಾಲೆಗೆ ಹಾಕಿದರೆ ಹಳದಿ ಹೊಳಪು ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ; ತಾಮ್ರ ಹಸಿರು ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಧಾತುವೂ ಬೆರಳಚ್ಚಿನಂತೆ ತನ್ನದೇ ರೇಖೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೈಡ್ರೋಜನ್ ರೇಖೆಗಳಿಂದ ಬೋರ್ ತಮ್ಮ ಮಾದರಿಯನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸಿದರು.

body.en: Atoms emit light only at certain wavelengths, giving a line spectrum. For hydrogen the lines fit the Rydberg equation. The Lyman series ($n_1$ = 1) is in the UV, the Balmer series ($n_1$ = 2) in the visible, and the Paschen ($n_1$ = 3), Brackett ($n_1$ = 4) and Pfund ($n_1$ = 5) series in the infrared.
body.kn: ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ತರಂಗಾಂತರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೆಳಕು ಹೊರಸೂಸುತ್ತವೆ—ರೇಖಾ ರೋಹಿತ. ಲೈಮನ್ ಸರಣಿ UVಯಲ್ಲಿ, ಬಾಮರ್ ಸರಣಿ ಗೋಚರ ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪಾಶನ್, ಬ್ರಾಕೆಟ್, ಫಂಡ್ ಸರಣಿಗಳು IRನಲ್ಲಿ.

narration.en: Atoms give out light only at certain wavelengths. For hydrogen, the Lyman series is in the ultraviolet, the Balmer series is visible, and the Paschen, Brackett and Pfund series are in the infrared.
narration.kn: ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ತರಂಗಾಂತರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೆಳಕು ಹೊರಸೂಸುತ್ತವೆ—ರೇಖಾ ರೋಹಿತ. ಲೈಮನ್ ಸರಣಿ UVಯಲ್ಲಿ, ಬಾಮರ್ ಸರಣಿ ಗೋಚರ ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪಾಶನ್, ಬ್ರಾಕೆಟ್, ಫಂಡ್ ಸರಣಿಗಳು IRನಲ್ಲಿ.

title.en: Bohr's energy levels and spectral series

say.en: In Bohr's model the electron can have only certain energies. The levels crowd together as n increases and reach zero at n equals infinity.
Jumps down to n equals 1 give the Lyman series in the ultraviolet; jumps down to n equals 2 give the Balmer series, which we see as visible lines.
The energy of level n is minus 2.18 times 10 to the minus 18, times Z squared over n squared, joules. The emitted photon carries the energy difference.
Example: the first Balmer line, n equals 3 to 2. The wavenumber is 15 233 per centimetre, so the wavelength is about 656 nanometres, the red H-alpha line.

body.en: Bohr proposed that the electron moves in fixed circular orbits (stationary states) without radiating energy. Its angular momentum is quantised, $m_e vr = nh/2\pi$. Energy is absorbed or emitted only when it jumps between orbits: ΔE = hν. For a hydrogen-like species, $E_n$ = −2.18 × 10$^{-18}$ (Z$^2$/n$^2$) J and $r_n$ = 52.9 (n$^2$/Z) pm. The model fails for multi-electron atoms and cannot explain the Zeeman and Stark effects.
body.kn: ಬೋರ್ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳದೆ ಸುತ್ತುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಕಕ್ಷೆಯಿಂದ ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಜಿಗಿದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ ಅಥವಾ ಹೊರಸೂಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಮಾದರಿ ಬಹು-ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳಿಗೆ ವಿಫಲ.

points.en: Works only for one-electron species (H, He⁺, Li²⁺)

narration.en: Bohr said the electron moves in fixed orbits without losing energy, and gives out or takes in light only when it jumps between orbits. The energy of the nth orbit is minus 2.18 times ten to the minus 18 joules, times Z squared over n squared.
narration.kn: ಬೋರ್ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳದೆ ಸುತ್ತುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಕಕ್ಷೆಯಿಂದ ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಜಿಗಿದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ ಅಥವಾ ಹೊರಸೂಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಮಾದರಿ ಬಹು-ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳಿಗೆ ವಿಫಲ.

aim.en: To identify metal ions from the colours they give to a flame.

narration.en: Each metal ion gives a characteristic flame colour because its electrons jump back between fixed energy levels. This is the line spectrum you can see with your own eyes.

caption.en: The curve shows the energy of level n, −13.6/n² eV. Pick a jump from n₂ down to n₁ and read the wavenumber, wavelength and energy of the emitted light.

tryThis.en: Set n₁ = 2, n₂ = 3: the red Hα line near 656 nm.
Set n₁ = 1: every line is in the ultraviolet (Lyman series).
Make n₂ large: the lines crowd towards the series limit.

narration.en: The curve shows the energy of level n, −13.6/n² eV. Pick a jump from n₂ down to n₁ and read the wavenumber, wavelength and energy of the emitted light. Set n₁ = 2, n₂ = 3: the red Hα line near 656 nm.

problem.en: An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 5 to n = 2. Find the energy and wavelength of the light emitted.

steps.en: λ = 434 nm, a violet-blue line of the Balmer series.

steps.en: rₙ = 52.9 n²/Z pm with n = 1, Z = 2.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the radius of the first Bohr orbit of He⁺.

body.en: When electrons in many atoms fall from level n to the ground state, the maximum number of different lines is n(n − 1)/2. From n = 4: 4 × 3/2 = 6 lines. Between any two levels n₂ and n₁: (n₂ − n₁)(n₂ − n₁ + 1)/2.

narration.en: Counting spectral lines. When electrons in many atoms fall from level n to the ground state, the maximum number of different lines is n(n − 1)/2. From n = 4: 4 × 3/2 = 6 lines. Between any two levels n₂ and n₁: (n₂ − n₁)(n₂ − n₁ + 1)/2.
